text:
mark: Heads-up — onboarding lab: rotated API key, sampleapp immediately 401'd.
sophie: Error text?
mark: `401 Unauthorized: invalid key scope` from SDK. New hire swapped REDWOOD_API_KEY in CI but didn't have REDWOOD_PROJECT set.
ian: Are we mixing env names? sampleapp README lists REDWOOD_ORG and REDWOOD_API_KEY only.
celine: SDK parity issue: Python/Go look for REDWOOD_PROJECT; Node/Java still check REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME. CI injects REDWOOD_PROJECT. Dotfiles or baked .env sometimes contain REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME -> mismatch.
sophie: For short-term: make SDKs accept both env vars (prefer REDWOOD_PROJECT) and log which var used.
ian: Also change retry policy: treat 401/403 as auth failures (no retry) unless server includes `Retry-After` or `x-redwood-retryable-auth: true`.
mark: Add startup validation in sampleapp: if REDWOOD_API_KEY present and no project detected -> exit 1 with helpful hint and link to onboarding doc.
celine: Ops: add onboarding smoke CI that runs sampleapp with only REDWOOD_API_KEY to catch this class.
ops-bot: CI: onboarding-smoke #210 queued
sophie: Backend follow-up: can server add `x-redwood-expected-scope: project` and `x-redwood-provided-scope` headers when rejecting? That would make diagnosing trivial.
ian: Also propose a small `redwood doctor` CLI for devs to detect env collisions (.env vs process env) and deprecated vars like REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME.
mark: Timeline: docs + sampleapp check today; SDK parity + retry change in next patch; backend header ticket filed by @celine.
celine: I'll file the backend ticket and PR for sampleapp README now.  Assigning SDK work to @ian.
mark: Thanks. Follow-ups: PR links, CI pass, and update onboarding checklist.
